key_choices.text: For his first four Nations League games Klopp named 44 players, including 16 uncapped, and split them into two squads.
Joshua Kimmich kept the captain's armband under Klopp.
Klopp named Marc-André ter Stegen as Germany's number one goalkeeper 'for the moment'.
His first squad left out Deniz Undav, Leroy Sané and Oliver Baumann.

For the November window he cut the group to 24 and recalled Niclas Füllkrug. He also gave a first senior call-up to Wael Mohya and kept five recent debutants, including Jonas Urbig, Said El Mala and Philipp Treu.
At his unveiling Klopp said Germany would play with four defenders and rely on wingers, and that some players would get opportunities they did not expect.
Against the Netherlands Klopp started Ter Stegen; Treu, Schlotterbeck, Tah, Brown; Kimmich, Pavlovic; Gruda, Wirtz, Scherhant; Havertz.

links.text: Klopp's first match as Germany coach was against the Netherlands, then coached by another new man, Xavi. It ended 1-1 in Amsterdam, with Völler asking for patience.

Before the World Cup opener against Curaçao, Klopp, working as a TV pundit, said 'luckily Julian Nagelsmann picks the team – for now'. He later apologised on air, and a few weeks later he was named Nagelsmann's successor.
Germany lost 0-1 to Greece in Klopp's first home game, a defeat described as historic.
The 5-0 win over the Netherlands on 16 November 2026 sealed Germany's place in the Nations League quarter-finals. Al Jazeera called it the Dutch side's heaviest defeat in 67 years.

teams.appointed: Announced by the KNVB on 12 August 2026 (contract to the 2030 World Cup). He was presented in Zeist on 25 August 2026.
teams.replaced_reason: Koeman resigned on 30 June 2026, hours after the Netherlands lost on penalties to Morocco in the World Cup round of 32. He said the responsibility ultimately rests with the head coach.

title_options: How a 5-0 Hid a 1.39 to 1.11 Game
Germany 5-0 Netherlands: The Score Hides a Close Game
script.description:
Germany beat the Netherlands 5-0 in Berlin in the UEFA Nations League, but the expected goals read 1.39 to 1.11. We follow Klopp, Wirtz, Gruda and a Dutch back line that struggled, and ask how a 5-0 hid a game that close.

Quotes and context come from ESPN (quoting Klopp to ARD), Yahoo Sports, FIFA.com, the DFB and Al Jazeera. Photos via Wikimedia Commons under their stated licences. Data: FotMob.

shots.text: Olympiastadion, Berlin. Minute 25. Still 0-0.
Donyell Malen meets the ball with his head, right in front of goal. Expected goals, or xG, measures how likely a shot is to score. This one is worth 0.69. More likely a goal than not. He misses.
By the end, Germany have won 5-0. Yet the expected goals read 1.39 to 1.11. So how did a 5-0 hide a game that close?

shots.text: The first half belongs to Germany. The momentum graph has them on top for 72 percent of it.
But it is no siege. Havertz heads a set piece in minute 23, and it is saved. Scherhant hits the post in minute 32. And the best chance of the half is still Malen's miss.

Then, minute 41. Joshua Kimmich finds Derry Scherhant, who finishes with his right foot, from open play. The chance is worth 0.03 xG. Almost nothing. It goes in. 1-0. Germany take a scrap. The Dutch spurned a 0.69. Hold on to that.

shots.text: Here is what the scoreline hides. Data from FotMob gives expected goals of 1.39 for Germany and 1.11 for the Netherlands. Almost level.
The Dutch number rests on one header: Malen's, in minute 25. That single chance is 0.69 of the 1.11. Germany's five goals came from smaller chances: 0.03, 0.05, 0.13, 0.24 and 0.26.
Germany took the chances the Dutch spurned. They also shot more: 18 shots to 9, and 10 on target to 1. So it was not just luck. Germany shot more, and shot straighter.

So, the answer. This was a game close on chances that Germany won in the box, and the Dutch lost there. Germany had 50 touches in the opposition box, the Netherlands 19. And for Xavi, it all comes back to one header, Malen's 0.69 miss at minute 25.
Tell me in the comments: was Malen's miss the moment the night tipped? And if you like football told through the numbers, subscribe to The Other Touchline.

notes: Hook: "Germany will win this match 5-0. But was it really that one-sided?" spoils the result and then asks a weak question; open on the sharper contrast instead: a 0.69 chance missed at 0-0, then a 5-0 scoreline, with 'how did a 5-0 hide a 1.39 to 1.11 xG game?' as the question.

Scene 3 is a pause in the story: "Klopp is the first character... The third character is on the other side" reads like a cast list, and there is no second character. Cut the Klopp 'Wow, that was cool' quote here, or use it only as the closing payoff.

The Dumfries setup ("Remember his name") is never paid off: scene 6 says "the numbers cannot show" the rest of his night. Either cut the setup or build a real payoff on the 3.3 rating, such as the Dutch right side collapsing during the 60 to 78 minute goal run.

The Act One line "A chance worth just 0.03 xG. It goes in" is your best moment of data-as-story, but it is followed by a 5 goals vs 1.39 xG argument. Frame the thesis once as 'Germany took the chances the Dutch spurned' and stop repeating the 'not a massacre' point in scenes 7, 8 and 9.

Scene 2 is a dense list of coach histories, form and injuries before any action: "Xavi Hernández took over the Netherlands after Ronald Koeman resigned, hours after a shootout loss to Morocco." Trim it to one stakes line (two new coaches, 1-1 in Amsterdam, Germany needing the win) and move the injuries into a single short sentence.

The ending does not fully answer the opening question and then hedges: "Whether it is also 'Wow, that was cool' is for you to decide." End with a firm verdict, such as 'a close contest that Germany won in the box, and the Dutch lost there', tied back to Malen's 0.69 miss at minute 25.

shorts.title: Gruda's 9.2: One Goal, Two Assists in Berlin

shots.text: Brajan Gruda's 9.2 was the best rating on the pitch in Berlin.
Germany led 2-0 when his pass set up Schlotterbeck's header in the 65th minute. 3-0.
Six minutes later, Gruda set up Wirtz for the fourth. 4-0.
Then he scored himself, with his left foot, for 5-0. One goal, two assists.
Wirtz scored twice and was rated 9.0. Gruda still finished above him.
Klopp said, "I wouldn't have dared to wish for a 5-0 before the game." Who was your man of the match? Full story on the channel.

shorts.title: The 0.03 xG Goal That Cracked the Dutch

shots.text: Germany's first goal was worth just 0.03 xG.
Derry Scherhant had been blocked in the 13th minute and hit the post in the 32nd.
In the 41st minute Kimmich passed, Scherhant hit it with his right foot, and it was 1-0.
Germany were on top for 72% of that first half, with one goal to show for it.
That was the lowest xG of Germany's five goals. Four more came after the break, and it finished 5-0. Which goal changed the game for you? Full story on the channel.
